subject.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child

question: Should `sessions.create` permanently expose a caller-declared `succeedsParent` tri-state, including legacy omission semantics, now that merged Codex consumer logic already prevents the reported parent-binding failure?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but deciding which session creators may retire a parent is a gateway lifecycle and public protocol contract choice that source-level review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Adopt explicit succession
options.body: Approve `succeedsParent` as the gateway contract and require focused compatibility coverage for in-repo and external explicit-key callers.

options.title: Keep consumer hardening only
options.body: Retain the merged cross-key Codex protection and avoid adding a broader session-creation lifecycle API until another caller requires it.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit succession
recommendation.body: Approve `succeedsParent` as the gateway contract and require focused compatibility coverage for in-repo and external explicit-key callers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged lifecycle-hook work is the closest provenance for the parent/child hook semantics this API would formalize.
